newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen lower with cash, BPA sales.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen lower with cash, BPA sales.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading mostly lower Thursday in line with a dip in Western electricity physicals prices and the return of the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) to the surplus power sales arena, industry sources said.
BPA said it was offering up to 200 megawatts of firm power during heavy load hours on Friday and Saturday, after staying out of the surplus sales market for six days.

Western physical electricity prices were also reported to be dipping Thursday, with December California Oregon Border (COB) pegged at $22.50-23.40 and December Palo Verde (PV) assessed at $21.50-21.80 per megawatt hour (MWh).
Some downward pressure on electricity futures was also seen from mild weather through much of the West and a decline in spot natural gas prices, the sources said.
As of 1245 EST, December COB was trading down 85 cents at its highest level of the day at $22.90 after moving as low as $22.50 per MWh.
Traders said the December contract hit significant support at $22.50 in morning trade.
January COB was trading $1.02 lower at $20.10 after trade as low as $19.90 per MWh. February and March COB were also trading down 80 cents and $1.00 respectively.
December PV was trading down 15 cents at the day's high of $22.00 after moving as low as $21.40 per MWh, while January was down 60 cents at $18.90 after transactions as high as $19.50 per MWh.
NYMEX said that as of 1225 EST a total of 75 COB and 21 PV contracts had changed hands.
COB open interest for Nov 6 rose 23 to 3,942 while PV open interest rose 85 to 1,875, NYMEX said.
